result:
The subscription is now the single source of a workspace's plan, and the trial sweep only touches subscriptions still on trial. Typecheck passes and the full vitest suite passes (73 files, 617 tests).

Changes:

- **`src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts`**: `findOrgById`, `findOrgBySlug`, `listOrgsForUser`, `updateOrg` and `archiveOrg` overlay the subscription's plan onto the org. The `organizations.plan` column is only used when there is no subscription. Every quota, feature gate, displayed plan and webhook check reads `org.plan`, so they all follow the subscription.
- **`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`**: `consumeRateLimit` takes an optional `plan` argument, which scales the burst buckets. The `setOrgPlan` override is kept because an existing test uses it.
- **Rate-limit call sites** now pass the org's plan: `comment-service.ts`, `search-service.ts`, `invitation-service.ts`, `actions/comments/create-comment.ts` and `actions/members/invite-member.ts`. They get it from a new `getOrgPlan(orgId)` in `organization-service.ts`. I did not pass it to the anonymous auth and inbound-webhook limiters, which use the free default.
- **`src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts`**: `listTrialsEndingBefore` now also requires `status = 'trialing'`. A paid plan chosen during the trial becomes `active`, so it is no longer swept down. Running the sweep again still changes nothing, because swept subscriptions are on `free` and `active`.

I did not add a sync from the subscription to the `organizations.plan` column, since reads no longer depend on it.
